name: Yudhiṣṭhira
bio: Eldest Pāṇḍava, son of Dharma. Devoted to truth — and undone by the dice.

name: Bhīma
bio: Second Pāṇḍava, son of the wind. Immense strength, immense appetite, fierce in love and in anger.

name: Arjuna
bio: Third Pāṇḍava, son of Indra. The peerless archer to whom Kṛṣṇa spoke the Gītā.

name: Draupadī
bio: Born from the sacrificial fire, wife of the five Pāṇḍavas. Her question in the hall is never answered.

name: Kṛṣṇa
bio: Prince of the Yādavas, Arjuna’s friend and charioteer, worshipped as an avatar of Viṣṇu.

name: Karṇa
bio: Kuntī’s secret firstborn, raised by a charioteer. Generous beyond measure, loyal to Duryodhana until death.

name: Duryodhana
bio: Eldest Kaurava. Proud, generous to friends, consumed by envy of his cousins.

name: Duḥśāsana
bio: Second Kaurava. He dragged Draupadī into the hall.

name: Gāndhārī
bio: Queen of Hastināpura, blindfolded by choice for life; mother of a hundred sons.

name: Abhimanyu
bio: Arjuna’s son by Subhadrā, Kṛṣṇa’s nephew; the boy who broke into the Cakravyūha.

name: Nakula
bio: Fourth Pāṇḍava, Mādrī’s son by the twin Aśvins: the handsomest of the brothers, a master of horses and the sword.

name: Sahadeva
bio: Youngest Pāṇḍava, Nakula’s twin; quiet and learned, and the one who kills Śakuni.

name: Kuntī
bio: Pṛthā, Kṛṣṇa’s aunt, given in childhood to King Kuntibhoja. Mother of Karṇa in secret, and of Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma and Arjuna.

name: Bhīṣma
bio: Devavrata, son of Śantanu and Gaṅgā. His vow never to rule or marry gave him his name, ‘the terrible’. Grandsire to both sides.

name: Droṇa
bio: A brahmin master of arms who teaches the Kuru princes, and fights for the Kauravas to the end. Father of Aśvatthāmā.

name: Dhṛtarāṣṭra
bio: The blind king of Hastināpura, father of the hundred Kauravas. He sees what is right and cannot hold his son to it.

name: Vidura
bio: Vyāsa’s son by a palace servant, said to be Dharma born as a man. Minister to the blind king, and the voice of plain truth at court.

name: Śantanu
bio: King of the Kurus. Father of Bhīṣma by Gaṅgā, and of two short-lived sons by Satyavatī.

name: Gaṅgā
bio: The river goddess. For a time Śantanu’s wife, and mother of Bhīṣma.

name: Satyavatī
bio: Raised by a fisher chief on the Yamunā, she becomes the Kuru queen. Before her marriage she bore the sage Vyāsa.

name: Vyāsa
bio: Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana: Satyavatī’s son by the sage Parāśara, father of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu and Vidura, and the poet who composed the epic.

name: Ambā
bio: Eldest princess of Kāśī. Carried off by Bhīṣma and then refused by everyone, she lives only for his death, and is born again as Śikhaṇḍī.

name: Pāṇḍu
bio: ‘The pale one’: Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s younger brother and king in his place. Father in name of the five Pāṇḍavas.

name: Mādrī
bio: Princess of Madra, Pāṇḍu’s second wife, mother of Nakula and Sahadeva.

name: Śakuni
bio: Gāndhārī’s brother, a master of dice and Duryodhana’s closest counsellor.

name: Śalya
bio: King of Madra and brother of Mādrī; tricked into fighting for Duryodhana, he drives Karṇa’s chariot and leads the last day.

name: Aśvatthāmā
bio: Droṇa’s only son, born with a jewel in his forehead. After the war he raids the sleeping camp, and is cursed to wander.

name: Kṛpa
bio: A brahmin warrior who teaches the Kuru princes before Droṇa; one of the few on either side to survive the war.

name: Drupada
bio: King of Pāñcāla: Droṇa’s boyhood friend and later his enemy; father of Draupadī, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍī.

name: Dhṛṣṭadyumna
bio: Born from Drupada’s sacrificial fire to kill Droṇa; commander of the Pāṇḍava army.

name: Śikhaṇḍī
bio: Drupada’s child, born a daughter and later a man: Ambā born again. Arjuna shoots at Bhīṣma from behind Śikhaṇḍī.

name: Ghaṭotkaca
bio: Bhīma’s son by the rākṣasī Hiḍimbā; huge, magical and always loyal to his father’s family.

name: Subhadrā
bio: Kṛṣṇa’s sister, Arjuna’s wife and Abhimanyu’s mother.

name: Virāṭa
bio: King of Matsya, who shelters the Pāṇḍavas in their hidden year without knowing who they are.

name: Uttarā
bio: Virāṭa’s daughter, Abhimanyu’s wife, and mother of Parīkṣit.

name: Parīkṣit
bio: Abhimanyu’s son, born dead and brought to life by Kṛṣṇa; king of the Kurus after the Pāṇḍavas.

name: Janamejaya
bio: Parīkṣit’s son: the king at whose great sacrifice the whole epic is first told.

name: Sañjaya
bio: Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s charioteer and counsellor, given the sight to see the whole war and tell it to the blind king.

name: Balarāma
bio: Kṛṣṇa’s elder brother, who taught the mace to both Bhīma and Duryodhana and would take no side.

name: Jayadratha
bio: King of Sindhu, husband of the Kauravas’ sister Duḥśalā. He holds the Cakravyūha shut on the day Abhimanyu dies.

name: Duṣyanta
bio: A king of the Paurava line, ancestor of the Kurus.

name: Śakuntalā
bio: Daughter of the sage Viśvāmitra and the apsaras Menakā, raised in Kaṇva’s hermitage; mother of Bharata.

name: Ekalavya
bio: A Niṣāda prince who taught himself archery before a clay image of Droṇa.

name: Hiḍimbā
bio: A rākṣasī of the forest who chooses Bhīma; mother of Ghaṭotkaca.

name: Maya
bio: The asura architect, spared from the Khāṇḍava fire, who builds the Pāṇḍavas a hall of wonders.

name: Jarāsandha
bio: King of Magadha, born in two halves, enemy of Kṛṣṇa’s people.

name: Śiśupāla
bio: King of Cedi and Kṛṣṇa’s cousin, who was promised a hundred insults’ grace.

name: Hanumān
bio: The monkey hero of the Rāmāyaṇa, son of the wind, and so Bhīma’s elder brother.

name: Urvaśī
bio: An apsaras of Indra’s heaven.

name: Kīcaka
bio: Commander of Virāṭa’s army and brother of the queen.

name: Uttara
bio: Virāṭa’s young son, who boasts of fighting the Kurus and then has to be driven to battle.

name: Kṛtavarman
bio: A Yādava chief who fights for Duryodhana and joins the night raid.

name: Babhruvāhana
bio: Arjuna’s son by Citrāṅgadā, king of Maṇipura.

name: Ulūpī
bio: A nāga princess, one of Arjuna’s wives.

name: Jarā
bio: The hunter whose arrow ends Kṛṣṇa’s life.

name: Takṣaka
bio: A king of the serpents.

name: Āstīka
bio: A young brahmin, half nāga by his mother, who stops the snake sacrifice.

name: Vaiśampāyana
bio: Vyāsa’s pupil, who first recites the epic at Janamejaya’s sacrifice.

name: Ugraśravas
bio: The bard who heard Vaiśampāyana and retells the epic to the sages of Naimiṣa.

name: Śaunaka
bio: Head of the sages at the long sacrifice in the Naimiṣa forest.
